name: fetch-requests-in-hooks-always-need-timeout
hook: useCurrentUser had no timeout on its fetch call
body:
When a fetch request is made in a useEffect hook (like useCurrentUser's fetchUser), it can hang indefinitely if the server doesn't respond. This causes isLoading to stay true forever, showing a loading spinner forever.

Fix: Use AbortController with a setTimeout to abort the request after a reasonable timeout (e.g., 15s).

**Why:** This bug (#2503) manifested as the /admin/lesson-duplications/<id> page showing 'Loading…' forever because the useCurrentUser fetch to /api/users/me had no timeout and no way to abort. This is the same pattern as the prior bug #1822, which proves this lesson needs to be applied universally: ANY useEffect fetch without a timeout is a latent bug.
why: The same pattern (fetch in useEffect with no timeout) caused two separate bugs (#1822 and #2503). A lint rule or automated check should prevent this going forward.
